title: Accurate Industrial Anomaly Detection and Localization Using Weakly-Supervised Residual Transformers (WeakREST)
mechanism: Residual between each test patch feature and its nearest normal patch feature (PosFAR) is fed to a supervised Swin segmenter; works with pixel, box or image labels.
adaptation: Memory banks from house-clean pool cells per source x layout (mono, multi, multi half-cut from 1,152 pool half-cells). Features from house ResNet-34 layer1/layer2 (stride 4/8) so residuals align with U-Net++ skips; residual 1x1-projected to 16 ch and added to decoder at 1/4 and 1/8. 24-class labels unchanged. Half-cut banks make scuff 'normal' in the residual, so the prior targets cracks on E1.
evidence: R: MVTec AD supervised AP 87.6 (prior best 86.0); box-only labels AP 87.1; also MVTec 3D, KSDD2, Real-IAD. No thin-label evidence.
min_experiment: Offline: fraction of crack components >=20 px missed by PF ensemble (p<0.001) that fall in top 1% residual norm on F51 + CV val; kill if <30%. Then arm PF + residual injection vs PF, 5 seeds, module-grouped 5-fold CV then E1 once. Metrics: CV crack relF1@2, inactive IoU, E1 crack relF1@2 and recall in 20 scuff half-cut cells. Kill: E1 relF1@2 gain < +0.03 and CV inactive gain < +0.02, or CV crack IoU drop > 0.01. Extra arm: bank without half-cells.
prior_overlap: none. BRIEF section 5 lists anomaly-detection priors as never tried; pool feature learning (MIM, DDeP) is a different mechanism.
